facts.text: On this date in 1947, India and Pakistan became independent simultaneously — the same midnight moment, the same colonial withdrawal, two nations born from a single breath.
On August 15, 1971, Nixon ended the U.S. dollar's convertibility to gold, untethering every currency on Earth from a fixed anchor in a single Sunday-night broadcast.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka with a 4,000 km radius than outside it — that ring captures roughly half the entire human population.
The city of Jakarta is sinking so fast in some districts that buildings constructed in the 1990s now have their ground floors permanently underwater.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding about 60% of the world's total freshwater lake surface area.
On this date in 1971, Nixon severed the dollar's last link to gold, ending Bretton Woods. The 'temporary' measure is now 55 years permanent.
On August 15, 1982, the Dow Jones closed at 776. It has since risen over 5,000%.
The U.S. penny costs about 3.7 cents to manufacture. The government loses money on every one it mints.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — yet the company sold less than 2% of itself. The float was smaller than many mid-cap stocks.
Japan's Government Pension Investment Fund manages $1.5 trillion, making it the largest single pool of retirement money on earth.

On this date in 1977, the Big Ear radio telescope received the 'Wow! signal' — a 72-second burst from space so perfectly matching expected alien transmission patterns that the astronomer circled it and wrote 'Wow!' No source has ever been found.
On August 15, 1960, Joe Kittinger fell from 102,800 feet and briefly reached 614 mph — faster than sound — without a vehicle, just a pressure suit and gravity.
Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, your bones completely replace themselves through a process called remodeling, meaning the femur you were born with is entirely gone.
A neutron star teaspoon weighs roughly a billion tons. The entire Sun, compressed to that density, would fit inside a city.
The human eye can detect a single photon in total darkness. Your visual system is operating at the physical limit of what light allows.

On this day in 1945, Japan announced its surrender — the first time most Japanese citizens had ever heard the Emperor's voice, broadcast on radio in a dialect so formal many couldn't understand the words.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
On this day in 1971, Nixon ended the gold standard in a Sunday night TV address so sudden that his own Treasury staff learned about it from the broadcast.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and lost. Linguists consider it untranslatable — even Brazilians use it to describe missing things that never existed.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. The word carries grief, belonging, and incompleteness in a single breath.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. One of the world's most succinct words for a universal human moment.

On this date in 1945, Emperor Hirohito's recorded surrender address introduced most Japanese citizens to a word: 'gyokuon-hoso,' meaning 'broadcast of the jeweled voice.' It was the first time many had ever heard him speak.
Apricity: the warmth of winter sun on skin. Coined by Henry Cockeram in 1623 and then abandoned by English entirely — a perfectly useful word left to die for no good reason.

On August 15, 2017, Bitcoin Cash completed its first block after the hard fork — block 478,559, mined nine hours after the split, a delay that exposed just how little hashrate the new chain had initially secured.
On August 15, 2012, BitInstant processed its 1,000th same-day Bitcoin purchase. The company would be shut down eighteen months later after its CEO was arrested for laundering funds through Mt. Gox.
Ethereum's gas limit is not set by the protocol — it is a rolling median negotiated by miners and validators each block, meaning network throughput is a social consensus, not a hard rule.
The Bitcoin genesis block contains $50 in BTC that is permanently unspendable: Satoshi hard-coded the coinbase transaction in a way that early Bitcoin clients could not include it in the UTXO set.

Uniswap v2 introduced a 0.05% protocol fee switch that has never once been turned on — every dollar of the billions in fees collected has gone entirely to liquidity providers, not the protocol treasury.

On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet. It won by a 10.8-point margin — so large that organizers initially suspected an error. Deep learning's takeover of computer vision began with that suspicion.

On August 15, 2023, Meta released Llama 2 publicly under a commercial license, making a 70-billion-parameter model free to download. Within 72 hours it had been fine-tuned, quantized, and run on a laptop.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. homes, spent in a matter of weeks.
Transformers were not designed for language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation; the authors expected the architecture to remain a niche tool for sequence tasks.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback requires surprisingly few labels. InstructGPT, which reshaped how aligned models are trained, used roughly 40,000 human-labeled examples — fewer than many undergraduate datasets.
